Subject: Midterm Capacity Lift & Rateband Adjustment Request

Hi Samantha —

Quick note following our Q3 review: ShopFlux exceeded the current hosted monthly commit in September and we anticipate continued elevated usage during the holiday pilot. To avoid throttling and to keep unit costs predictable, we'd like to propose a midterm amendment that: 

- Increases the monthly committed tokens from 2.5B -> 4.0B (effective Nov 1)
- Adds a temporary peak-rateband for 9am–1pm PST (+10% unit price during the window) to reserve capacity at scale
- Provides a one-time credit to offset partial-month proration for November

Attached is a short summary and a CSV with observed Q3 usage patterns. High level ask: can we get procurement sign-off by next Wednesday (10/27) so we can schedule the capacity reservation before Black Friday test run?

Next steps we propose:
1) You review the amendment draft (attached)
2) Procurement signals approval and returns PO or DocuSign
3) We push the commit change on Nov 1 with monitoring playbook + Ops runbook

If useful we can schedule a 20-minute call this week to walk the numbers — Vanessa will join for ops handoff and Karthik for pricing+billing.

Thanks,

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Exec, Large Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick questions from procurement and engineering before we loop legal: 

1) Proration: how will the November credit be calculated? We have usage spikes on the first few days of the month for other vendors.
2) Peak-rateband: can you share what triggers the +10% price (absolute token count per minute or percent of capacity)?
3) SLA: will the commit increase change latency SLAs for our account during the peak window? We need to ensure any changes don’t impact the customer-facing SLA.

We can do a 30-min call Thursday morning (10/21) at 9:30am ET if that works — I’ll bring our infra lead.

Best,

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Midterm Capacity Lift & Rateband Adjustment Request

Looping internal ops and pricing notes here before the call with ShopFlux. Quick points to prep: 

- Proration approach: propose pro-rata credit = ((new_commit - old_commit)/new_commit) * monthly_fee * (days_remaining/30). Simple and defensible; we should confirm with finance.
- Peak-rateband trigger: implement as capacity reservation rule — charge +10% when request routing places >85% of reserved pool RPS in the 30-second rolling window. Ops will auto-throttle non-committed routes first.
- SLA: no change to latency SLA; provide explicit fallback paths to alternative model variants if queueing exceeds threshold. Ops to produce runbook.

Mateo: can you draft a short amendment with the above language and include the proration formula? Karthik: pricing redline if you think margin impact needs alternate structuring. I’ll draft the ops runbook and the playbook for the Nov 1 cutover.

- V

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Samantha —

Following our call earlier today, attached is the formal amendment draft and a short timeline. Highlights in the doc: 

- Effective date: 2027-11-01
- Commit change: 2.5B -> 4.0B monthly committed tokens
- Peak-rateband: 9:00–13:00 PST; +10% unit price when per-pool utilization >85% over a 30s rolling window
- Proration credit: applied to the November invoice using the formula Vanessa suggested (see section 2.3)
- Ops commitments: canary rollout 11/01–11/03, 24/7 on-call for first week, and automatic fallback to model-variant L2 if latency > 300ms median

Attachment includes a DocuSign link for signature and a consolidated pricing table for the amended term. Let me know if procurement needs a standalone PO line or if DocuSign is enough.
